card.name: Linking verbs before test-result descriptions
card.fires_on: Forms of "be" (is, are, were, be) or a tumor noun right after a medical subject, where the next word is likely to describe a finding or result, such as positive, negative, or abnormal.

modes.label: Verb after finding subject
modes.description: A form of be follows a subject such as lesions, polyps, or activity, before a result is stated.
modes.example: fundic gland polyps<< were>> identified incidentally on endoscopy.

modes.label: Auxiliary before a result
modes.description: The word be follows may or must or will not, before a finding is stated.
modes.example: NET tumors that do not bear somatostatin receptors will not<< be>> visualized.

modes.label: Inside tumor names
modes.description: The end of a tumor name such as carcinoma.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward saying positive or negative as the next word.
card.plain: It fires on words like "is" or "are" after an imaging or tumor finding, when a positive or negative result is likely to come next.
